mode: verbatim ingest through memory_append (one topic file per memory, global scope, fixed entry heading), no model, no embeddings; layered memory, keyword recall and the topic index at their defaults
how: memory_append.execute({section, content, topic}) per memory; ranked = memory_search.execute({query, limit:10}) (searchTopics: query terms = word runs and Han character bigrams, score = 4 per term in key+title, 2 per term in summary, 1 per term in body; ties by key); deployed = the soul:recall block: searchTopics(topics, userMessage, limit 5) rendered as key/title/summary rows within 1600 characters, active from the second user message of a session
notes: Package: dsh-soul-md 0.12.5 (npm tarball), index.js imported unmodified; the plugin's one dependency (schemastery) installed from npm during the image build; host packages @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools and dsh-home-paths are stubbed (identity defineTool, a home path).

Write path: the model decides what to write and under which topic key, with a section heading. The adapter writes every memory verbatim into its own topic (key = the memory id, heading label 'note', global scope, no persona card). A product topic normally groups several entries; one memory per topic is the adapter's layout choice and makes each topic descriptor equal to one memory. Dates: memory_append stamps the heading with the current time; the clock (Date) is set to each memory's date (12:00 UTC + index seconds) while writing, and to the day after the last memory for all questions.

deployed = the keyword-recall block only (up to 5 topic descriptor rows, 1600 characters, no score threshold: any topic sharing one query term is listed). The plugin also keeps a standing topic index in the system prompt (query-independent, default indexMode all; here 105 of 240 topics fit its character share). That standing index is resident memory and is not part of deployed or ranked.

The plugin recalls from the second user message of a session; every question session first receives one fixed unrelated message. Each question uses a fresh session object (recall state is per session).

Recall rows carry the topic key (the memory id) and the descriptor; ids are read from the key. memory_search results are read the same way. The recall block returns rows without scores: deployed scores are rank-derived.
ms times the soul:recall provider only (it lists and reads every topic file through the plugin's mtime cache and scores them).
